culo.intro: All cards are dealt. First to run out is the President, last is the Asshole, and between rounds the ends swap cards.

setup.note: With 5 or 6 players two decks play better: more combinations to go round.

culo.tableFree: The table is clear: you open
culo.noMoves: You cannot answer that: you have to pass

goal.title: Goal
goal.text: Get rid of your cards before everyone else. First is the President; last is the Asshole.

turn.title: How a round goes
turn.1: All the cards are dealt out.
turn.2: The leader plays one or more cards of the same value.
turn.3: The next player answers with exactly the same number of cards and a higher value, or passes.
turn.4: You may pass even if you can play: passing is a decision too.
turn.5: When everyone else has passed, the last player to play takes the cards and opens the next trick.

values.title: Card values
values.text: Lowest to highest. The 5 of coins is the highest card, above the Ace, and cannot be played together with other fives.

roles.title: Places and roles
roles.1: First to run out is the President.
roles.3: Second-to-last is the Vice-Asshole, and last is the Asshole.
roles.4: With 3 players there are no vice roles: President, one neutral and Asshole.

exchange.title: Swap between rounds
exchange.1: The Asshole gives their 2 best cards to the President, who gives their 2 worst back.
exchange.2: The Vice-Asshole gives their best card to the Vice-President, who returns their worst.

tips.title: Ideas to play better
tips.1: Do not spend your high cards too early: save them to close an important hand.
tips.2: Opening with four or five cards leaves the others almost no answer.
tips.3: Passing is tactics too: sometimes it pays to keep the good play back.
tips.4: Watch who is about to run out before you open.

exchange.title: Swap
exchange.note: These cards change hands before the next round.

mentiroso.intro: The whole deck is dealt. In turn you put cards face down and say what they are: you may lie about the value, never about the count. Anyone can doubt you, and whoever runs out of cards wins the hand.
mentiroso.claimPrompt: What do you say they are?
mentiroso.retireHint: You hold all four cards of one value: you may show them and take them out of the game.
mentiroso.handEnd: {{name}} is out of cards and wins the hand!

log.lie: It was a lie: {{name}} takes {{count}} cards

rules.title: How to play
rules.goal: You win a hand by running out of cards. The match goes to several hands.
rules.round: You put one or more cards face down and say what they are. Whoever opens the round sets the value and the rest follow it: you may lie about the value, not about the count.
rules.challenge: Anyone —not just the next player— can shout “liar!”. If it was a lie, the one who played takes the pile; if it was true, the doubter takes it. Either way, whoever takes the pile opens the next round.
rules.out: Once a player is out of cards they can no longer be doubted: the play that empties a hand is free.
rules.four: If you hold all four cards of one value you may show them and set them aside: they are no use to you any more.

brisca.intro: Three cards are dealt and the next one is turned up, marking the trump. Each player plays a card —there is no obligation to follow suit— and the highest trump wins. The winner takes the trick, draws first and leads. At the end, everyone adds up the value of their cards.
brisca.trumpGone: The turned-up card has already been picked up
brisca.trickEmpty: Nobody has played in this trick yet
brisca.swapHint: You won the trick and hold the seven of trump: you may take the turned-up card.
brisca.void: Tied at 60: the game is void

log.swap: {{name}} swaps the trump for the seven

rules.title: How to play
rules.goal: The match goes to whoever wins the agreed number of games. A game is won by scoring more points than your opponent with the cards from the tricks you take.
rules.order: The card order is not the deck's: low to high it is 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, Jack, Knight, King, 3, Ace. The three is the second highest card.
rules.trick: Three cards are dealt and the next one is turned up, marking the trump. Each player plays whatever card they like: there is no obligation to follow suit or to play trump. The highest trump wins, or if there is no trump, the highest card of the suit that led.
rules.draw: The winner of the trick takes the cards, draws first and leads the next one. The card that marks the trump is the last one drawn.
rules.swap: Whoever wins a trick may swap the turned-up card for the seven of that suit, before drawing and never after the penultimate trick.
rules.score: Counting: Ace 11, three 10, king 4, knight 3, jack 2; the rest are worth nothing. If both reach 60 points, the game is void.

tute.intro: The classic tute. Eight cards each and the rest in the stock: while cards remain to be dealt you only have to follow trump; once the stock runs out you must follow suit, beat the trick and trump. King and horse of the same suit sing: 40 if they are trump (las cuarenta) and 20 if not (las veinte), but only after winning a trick. First to 101 points wins, or whoever sings a tute.
tute.mustFollow: The stock is empty: you must follow suit, beat the trick and trump.
tute.mustTrump: While the stock lasts, only trump is compulsory.

log.tute: {{name}} has a tute and wins the game!

rules.title: How to play tute
rules.goal: First to 101 points wins, adding up the cards from the tricks you take, the acuses you sing and the 10 for the last trick.
rules.must: While the stock has cards you only have to follow trump, and you need not beat it. Once the stock is empty you must follow suit, beat the trick and trump: if you can follow suit you must, and if you can beat the highest card on the table you must too; if you have none of that suit, you must play trump.
rules.sing: King and horse of the same suit are worth 40 points if they are trump (las cuarenta) and 20 if they are another suit (las veinte). They can only be sung after winning a trick, one per trick.
rules.tute: All four kings or all four horses in hand are a tute: sing it and you win the game instantly.
rules.last: The last trick is worth 10 points and settles ties.

mus.intro: Four-handed mus in pairs: you play with the person opposite (seats 0 and 2 against 1 and 3). No trump and no suits, and with eight kings and eight aces: the three is worth the same as the king and the two the same as the ace. First you ask whether there is mus; then you bet on grande, chica, pairs and juego. The pair that reaches 40 stones wins, and a vaca is the best of three games.
mus.ordago: Órdago! The whole vaca is at stake

rules.title: How to play mus
rules.goal: The first pair to 40 stones wins. Each hand is played over four rounds, and in each round you can bet: if the bet is declined, whoever made it takes one stone.
rules.order: There is no trump and no suits. From highest to lowest: king or three, horse, jack, seven, six, five, four, two or ace: the three is worth the same as the king and the two the same as the ace ("eight kings and eight aces").
rules.mus: Before anything else you ask whether there is mus, starting with the dealer. As soon as one player cuts, nobody else discards and the rounds begin.
rules.lances: The four rounds go in this order: high card, low card, pairs and game (31 or more). In the game the order is 31, 32, 40, 37, 36, 35, 34 and 33: 31 is the best. If nobody has game, it goes to points: closest to 30 wins.
rules.bets: In each round you pass or bet, with two stones minimum. The opponent can accept, decline, raise or call órdago, which puts the whole vaca at stake. In pairs the highest bet of the two partners counts.
rules.pairs: In pairs, double pairs (two pairs or four of a kind) beat three of a kind, which beats a pair. Ties go to the highest card in the combination.
